blockers.issue: UART1MPRTOLEnable (0x14B4): Both parameters are UINT8[16] (16-byte raw bitmask arrays, per bms_v1_1_manifest.json and confirmed against the PDF -- p.12, 'UINT8 16 R'), not a scalar numeric or a text string. This project's canonical schema (protocol/schema/register-source.schema.json) supports wire_type U8/S8/U16/S16/U32/S32/F32/ASCII/BIT -- ASCII is the only multi-byte-array type available, and its real decode (jk_poll_scheduler_core.h's decode_ascii()) copies raw bytes VERBATIM into a display string with no hex-encoding -- safe for genuine text (device_model etc.) but NOT safe for an arbitrary 16-byte bitmask, which may contain embedded null bytes (truncating the displayed string early) or non-printable control bytes (rendering unpredictably in HTML/JS). No safe RAW hex-string representation exists in this project's decode primitives today -- inventing per-byte semantics for the bitmask (which bit means which protocol) was also explicitly out of scope this round. A genuine architecture gap, not an evidence gap: both the address and the wire type/length are already confirmed.
blockers.evidence_needed: Not evidentiary. Needed: a new decode primitive (e.g. decode_hex_string(), parallel to decode_ascii()/decode_exact_decimal()) that formats N raw bytes as a hex string ("AA BB CC ..."), safe for arbitrary binary content, plus the corresponding wire_type/domain plumbing through generate.js/generate_read_plan.js and its own unit tests -- a real, reviewable engineering task, not a one-line fix.
blockers.closure_criterion: decode_hex_string() (or equivalent) is implemented and unit-tested, this field gets a real canonical entry using it, and it classifies implemented_read.
blockers.resolution: Stage 3 continuation pass (2026-09-20, user-directed): decode_hex_string() (components/jk_poll_scheduler/jk_poll_scheduler_core.h) implements a safe, deterministic, bounds-checked byte-to-hex-string projection -- uppercase hex, space-separated, no ASCII assumption, never truncates on embedded 0x00, never loses 0xFF, fixed 16-byte length, unit-tested. A real canonical field now exists using it (wire_type HEX), published as a text_sensor, read-only, no write path. This is a raw, undecoded hex dump -- per-bit protocol semantics are still NOT claimed (dynamic_dependency.resolved=false, matching this project's own policy against inventing bitmask meanings).

blockers.parameter_id: total_voltage_raw,current_raw (ESPHome entities: total_voltage, current, power, charging_power, discharging_power, charging_current, discharging_current)
blockers.issue: CONFIRMED SOFTWARE DEFECT, found and fixed 2026-09-20 (hardware acceptance, second attempt, post-reflash, HEAD aded697): the 2026-09-19 generic exact-length response validation (data.size() != payload_bytes, tools/protocol/generate_read_plan.js) was applied unconditionally to every block, including the one CLUSTERED_GAP_AWARE custom-decode block at this address, whose payload_bytes=12 was only ever proven as the DECODE function's own read length (unit/golden-vector tests), never as this device's true wire response byte count -- that byte count remains the same open question as this block's register_count (10 vs 12 vs other candidates, never hardware-proven either way; see this block's own exceptionReason in generate_read_plan.js's CUSTOM_DECODE_BLOCKS table). On real hardware, this caused total_voltage/current (and every entity this block feeds) to read unavailable (NA) continuously for the ENTIRE observation window (>2.5h, confirmed fresh boot, uptime growing monotonically with zero reboots, re-verified independently via 2 separate EventSource reconnects) -- a 100% response-rejection rate -- while every OTHER block on the identical validator succeeded throughout. Downstream symptom: text_sensor/topology state=MISMATCH, reason=VOLTAGE_SUM_DIFFERS (jk_topology's own cross-check against the never-successfully-decoded total_voltage; jk_topology's own code was independently confirmed untouched by any Stage 3 commit this round, ruling it out as an independent defect). FIX APPLIED THIS ROUND: this block's response-length validation reverted to a floor check (data.size() >= payload_bytes) via a new per-block jk_poll_scheduler::Block::strict_length flag (false only for this block, true for every other block, which keeps the stricter, individually-audited exact-match policy) -- restoring exactly the tolerant validation this literal was actually hardware-validated under before the 2026-09-19 change. Regression coverage: test/jk_poll_scheduler/test_read_plan_decode.cpp's test_strict_length_carve_out_for_clustered_gap_aware_block(), plus updated assertions in test/protocol_catalog/test_generic_read_plan_register_count.js and test_projection_decoder.js. This fix is SOFTWARE-ONLY and requires a new firmware build+flash to take effect on the device that produced this evidence -- it was NOT live on the device during this hardware-acceptance session.
blockers.evidence_needed: A real FC03 capture at 0x1290 (request register_count=12, as currently issued) showing the device's actual raw response byte length -- this is the same hardware-pending question this block's own exceptionReason has carried since before this round (10 vs 12 vs some other candidate). With the floor-check fix now deployed, read-only confirmation that total_voltage/current successfully and repeatedly decode non-NA values on a new firmware build is the immediate, lower-bar acceptance evidence; a byte-exact FC03 capture is the deeper evidence needed to eventually tighten this block back to an exact-match check (or to correct register_count/payload_bytes with real proof, per this project's own no-fabricated-derivation policy).
blockers.closure_criterion: EITHER: (a) a real FC03 capture at 0x1290 definitively establishes the device's true response byte length, closing the underlying register_count/payload_bytes ambiguity and allowing this block to be reclassified with hardware-proven values (potentially restoring strict_length=true if the true length is proven to exactly equal a corrected payload_bytes); OR (b) at minimum, a subsequent hardware-acceptance session on a NEW firmware build (containing this round's strict_length fix) confirms total_voltage/current read live, non-NA values repeatedly and without regression, which closes the immediate defect this blocker was opened for even if the deeper register_count question stays open under a separate, narrower blocker scope at that point.
